definition: An adaptive behavior scale is an assessment measure used to rate a person’s adaptive behavior, such as in autism research and clinical outcome tracking. In this packet, the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scale (VABS-3) is used to record baseline functioning and changes over time.

reasons: The packet supports use of the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scale (VABS-3) as an input for baseline functioning and monthly change in an autism-spectrum-disorder outcomes model, but it does not define “adaptive behavior scale” as a general assessment measure.
The added generalization to “autism research and clinical outcome tracking” is broader than what the packet states and is not supported as a definition of the term.

The definition claims the scale is used in “clinical outcome tracking,” but the packet only describes using VABS-3 as input for a cost-effectiveness model (baseline VABS-3 and monthly VABS-3 changes), not outcome tracking in a clinical sense.

The definition is placed under the field “diagnosis,” but the packet describes VABS-3 as an input reflecting adaptive behavior outcomes in an autism model, not as a diagnostic concept or diagnostic criterion.
